metaDescription: Six Litheli cordless snow blowers and shovels compared by path width, battery system and snow depth, from a 12-inch shovel to a 21-inch blower.
expertTake: The 21-inch 40V blower with two 5Ah packs is the strongest Litheli for a real driveway, while the 20-inch 2x20V models are the budget way to start on the 20V platform. The two shovels are for steps and short walks only. Skip this brand for long, deep or gravel drives. If you only need one tool, buy the 21-inch blower and use a broom on the steps.
introParagraphs: Value-priced cordless snow tools are easy to find, and the hard part is working out which ones are real machines and which are small shovels with a motor. Both have their place, but they solve very different problems.

Models in this class share a basic recipe: a brushless motor, a rubber or steel auger and two small batteries working together. The differences show up in clearing width, snow depth per pass and how many packs the kit includes. Reading the kit contents carefully saves the most common disappointment, a machine that arrives without enough battery.

products.name: Litheli 40V 21-inch brushless snow blower, 2 x 5Ah
products.description:
This is the widest and deepest-clearing Litheli blower, a 21-inch single-stage with a 12-inch snow depth. Two 5Ah packs give a stated runtime of up to 30 minutes and about six parking spaces per charge, which is a meaningful step up from the 4Ah kits.

The key tradeoff against the 20-inch 40V model is 1 inch of path width and the larger batteries, with the 21-inch design adding a bit more weight. Compared with the wheeled 20-inch 2x20V, it uses a different battery system, so you cannot share packs between them.

It is a wheeled walk-behind machine with LED lighting and an ergonomic handle, which makes pre-dawn clearing easier. Keep the packs warm until the first pass and wipe the auger housing after each use so slush does not freeze in place. A practical check before buying is your longest clearing session: if a storm usually takes you more than 30 minutes, plan on a second set of packs or a rest while the first set recharges. On sloped drives, the lack of wheel drive means the operator supplies all the forward push, so keep the load light.
products.bestFor: Single-stage clearing of paved driveways up to a few cars wide.
cons: Single-stage will not cut through heavy berms
Packs do not interchange with the 20V kits

products.name: Litheli 40V 20-inch cordless brushless snow blower, 4Ah
products.description:
The 20-inch 40V is a brushless single-stage that clears 20 inches wide and 12 inches deep and throws up to 20 feet. The throw figure is shorter than rivals quote, which matters on wide drives where you want to put snow far from the path.

A single 4Ah pack is a limit on a long drive. If you plan to run it for more than one battery's worth, budget for a second pack. Its walk-behind frame, smooth wheels and dual LED headlights are the same practical package as the 21-inch model.

It is the right size for a one- or two-car drive. For anything beyond that, the 21-inch kit with two packs is the better choice. Because the kit ships with one pack, buyers who expect a long clear should price a second 40V pack alongside the machine, otherwise the break between passes is as long as the charge time.
products.bestFor: One- to two-car paved drives where a single pack is enough.
pros: Brushless motor with gas-like torque claims

products.name: Litheli 2x20V 20-inch cordless snow blower, 2 x 4Ah
products.description:
This version uses two 20V packs to make a 40V system, which lets it share batteries with Litheli's 20V tools. It clears a 20-inch path 12 inches deep and throws up to 25 feet, a few feet farther than the single-battery 40V model.

Its big advantage is that the two packs are a conventional 20V size, so you can borrow them from a drill or leaf blower. The downside is that two packs in series run out together, so there is no hot-swap trick to extend runtime without carrying extra pairs.

Walk-behind wheels, a 180-degree chute and LED headlights complete the package. Keep the packs warm and wipe the housing after use. Check the charger rating as well, since two 4Ah packs on a single small charger can take a long time to refill between storms.
products.bestFor: Owners who already have Litheli 20V batteries from other tools.
pros: Uses common 20V packs shared with other tools
cons: Both packs deplete at the same time
Not as wide as the 21-inch model

products.name: Litheli 2x20V 20-inch brushless snow blower with wheels
products.description:
This listing is the wheeled 20-inch 2x20V blower with a 180-degree adjustable chute and LED lights. It shares its specifications with the model above, so the decision comes down to the kit contents and availability.

Because the motor, auger and throw are comparable, think of the two 20-inch 2x20V listings as sibling versions of the same machine. If one comes with batteries you already have, take that one. The wheels make it easier to steer than a hand-carried shovel.

Expect to wipe snow and slush out of the chute after use, and to keep the packs out of the cold between jobs. Compare the box contents on the listing against the sibling model above, because accessories and battery counts are the only real difference between them.
products.bestFor: Wheeled convenience for a mid-sized paved drive.
cons: Specs match the other 20-inch 2x20V listing closely

products.name: Litheli 40V 13-inch brushless snow shovel, full loop handle
products.description:
The 13-inch shovel adds a 360-degree full-loop handle that lets you push with both hands in a more upright posture. It clears up to 7 inches deep and 13 inches wide and throws up to 25 feet, with a chute that rotates 30 degrees each way.

Two 20V 5Ah packs are rated for about 807 square feet, or roughly a 5-car driveway. That makes it viable for a short drive but not a long one, and it is the right tool for steps, porches and decks where a full blower will not fit.

Because it is a shovel-style tool, you carry some of the weight. Choose it if you value a narrow, light machine and an upright stance over speed. Because the loop handle changes your grip, try it on the stairs and the walk you actually clear; some people find the upright posture easier on the lower back, others prefer a conventional shovel grip.
products.bestFor: Short drives, porches and walks where an upright grip helps.
pros: Full loop handle allows an upright posture
Light enough to carry up steps
cons: Only 13 inches wide and 7 inches deep

products.name: Litheli 20V 12-inch cordless snow shovel, 4Ah
products.description:
This is the simplest tool in the group, a 9-pound 12-inch shovel on a single 20V 4Ah pack. It clears 12 inches wide and 6 inches deep and has an adjustable auxiliary handle.

It suits steps, decks and a short sidewalk, and it works well as a second tool for places the big blower cannot reach. Do not expect it to clear a driveway in one battery.

Treat it as a quick-reaction tool for light snow. In wet snow, pass lightly and clear in layers. At this weight it is easy to keep by the door, which means it actually gets used for a quick dusting, and that habit is the best reason to own one even if you also have a blower.
products.bestFor: Light snow on steps, decks and a short path.
pros: Quiet compared with a gas engine
cons: Only 12 inches wide and 6 inches deep
Single pack runs out quickly in heavy snow

buyingCriteria.explanation: Litheli sells 40V single-battery, 2x20V dual-pack and shovel-only systems. The 40V 21-inch kit uses two 5Ah packs, while the 2x20V models use two 4Ah 20V packs. If you own other 20V Litheli tools, the 2x20V version lets you reuse those packs. The mistake is assuming the two systems are interchangeable. If you already own a Litheli drill or trimmer, count those packs before buying, because the 2x20V version can save the cost of two batteries.

The 21-inch 40V clears 21 by 12 inches, the 20-inch models 20 by 12 and the shovels only 12 to 13 inches wide by 6 to 7 deep. For a drive more than one car wide, extra width translates directly into fewer passes. Mark your driveway width with a tape measure and divide by the path to count passes; the difference between 20 and 21 inches adds up over a long run.

The 21-inch kit is rated for about 30 minutes and six spaces. The 13-inch shovel's two 5Ah packs are rated for about 807 square feet. Plan to cut those figures when snow is wet or the pack is cold. The honest way to read these numbers is as a maximum for light powder; wet snow, cold packs and slopes can halve them.

Throw ranges from 20 feet on the single-pack 40V model to 25 feet on the 2x20V and shovels. Short throw means you must clear the same snow twice when wind or banks are against you. Wind direction changes the best chute angle, so a longer throw and a controllable chute together are worth more than either alone.

Every blower here has a single auger that scrapes the pavement. Heavy, crusty or deep snow stalls it, and gravel drives will throw stones. If your drive is gravel or heavily plowed, a two-stage is a better fit. A driveway that has been plowed by the city usually has a hard berm at the end, and a single-stage will not cut it; leave that to a shovel or a stronger machine.

Lithium packs lose output in deep cold. Store them indoors, insert them just before use and avoid leaving a charger in an unheated shed. This matters most with two-pack kits where both packs must be warm. Let a cold pack warm to room temperature before charging it, because charging at freezing temperatures can damage cells.

specDecoder.meaning: Two 20V packs are used together to make a 40V motor supply. Treat it as one 40V system that happens to use two small batteries.
specDecoder.watchFor: Both packs drain at the same rate, so you cannot swap one at a time.

specDecoder.meaning: One 40V battery powers the tool directly.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 20-inch 40V kit includes only one 4Ah pack.

specDecoder.meaning: No carbon brushes, so less wear and more efficiency.
specDecoder.watchFor: All six picks use brushless motors.

specDecoder.meaning: The maximum snow height the tool can take in one pass.
specDecoder.watchFor: 12 inches on the blowers versus 6 to 7 on the shovels.

specDecoder.meaning: An estimate of clearable area on a set of packs. It is a convenient comparison between shovels but varies a lot with snow type.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery system
howWeEvaluated.description: We sorted the lineup by 40V, 2x20V and shovel-only systems, since pack sharing decides ongoing cost. The 21-inch kit and 20-inch kits use different platforms. We noted what is in each box. This is the biggest cost factor over several winters.

howWeEvaluated.title: Clearing geometry
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared width and depth, 21 by 12 inches on the largest blower down to 12 by 6 on the smallest shovel. We treated depth as the limit on a single pass.

howWeEvaluated.title: Runtime claims
howWeEvaluated.description: We read stated figures such as 30 minutes and 807 square feet as best-case numbers. Based on the spec sheet, wet snow and cold packs will shorten them. Real runtime also depends on how hard you push the machine.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership burden
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed pack storage, charger care and cleaning the chute. Battery tools remove fuel work but add pack handling.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit to use
howWeEvaluated.description: We placed each tool in a role, blower, mid-size blower or shovel, rather than naming a single winner. This is an editorial assessment, not a measured score.

rows: Right width for a short run

howToChoose.note: Prices move, so compare current listing prices against your own driveway and the number of packs in the box before you decide.

cards.label: Blower
cards.text: The 21-inch 40V and 20-inch models roll on wheels and clear 12 inches deep. They suit driveways but are bulkier to store.

cards.label: Shovel
cards.text: The 13-inch and 12-inch shovels carry a share of the weight and clear narrow strips. They suit steps and short walks.

howToChoose.note: Choose a blower for a driveway and a shovel for steps; many owners end up with both.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A 20-inch path with a battery sized for the drive. A shorter drive needs fewer minutes, so a single 4Ah pack may be enough.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Litheli 40V 20-inch is the economical choice for one or two cars; the 21-inch adds runtime for a longer drive.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a longer drive or want a second set of packs. The 21-inch 40V kit includes two 5Ah packs. Longer clearing sessions also deserve a second charger so both pairs of packs are ready.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only clear steps or a short walk. The 12-inch shovel handles that with a single battery.

maintenance.why: Cold reduces output. Warm packs run longer and charge faster. A cold pack can also show a false low charge level, so let it settle before judging.
Slush freezes into ice. A quick wipe prevents jams.
Rubber or steel paddles wear and lose bite on the pavement. Replace paddles when the edge no longer touches the pavement across its full width.
A stalled auger can restart suddenly. Never use hands. Wait for the auger to stop completely before reaching in with a tool.
Full or empty storage shortens cell life. Check the charge every couple of months and top up if it has dropped.

faq.a: The 2x20V uses two common 20V packs that other Litheli tools share. The 40V uses a single pack or a pair of 5Ah packs. Choose by which platform you own. If you have no existing tools, the 21-inch 40V kit is the better standalone choice because the packs are bigger.

faq.q: Can a shovel clear a driveway?
faq.a: A 13-inch shovel can clear a short drive, but it takes many passes. For longer drives, a wheeled blower saves time and effort. For stairs and decks the shovel is actually more practical than a wheeled machine.

Wet snow drains packs faster and may stall a small auger. Clear in lighter passes and use the 21-inch for better headroom. Heavy snow also pulls more current, which shortens the battery by a third or more.
No. Single-stage augers throw loose stones. Use a two-stage with raised skid shoes. If your drive is part gravel, clear the paved section with the blower and use a shovel on the stones.
Yes for any drive more than a couple of cars. A second set lets one charge while you work. Rotate the packs so both age evenly.

faq.q: How do I store the machine?
faq.a: Remove packs, wipe the housing dry and store in a dry spot. Keep the charger indoors. Store the charger separately from the machine so moisture does not get into the contacts.
